narrativeReportMd:
# markdown R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard R4-to-R6 instance-breaking change was found for `markdown`. The local migration concerns are low-impact validator/code-generator issues: the effective `markdown.value` regex is widened to any non-empty string, and the R6 snapshot now identifies the primitive FHIR type metadata as `markdown` rather than `string`.

## Scope
The analysis compared the R4 and R6 `StructureDefinition-markdown.json` files, package indexes, package metadata, and related `string` and R4 `regex` StructureDefinitions. Inherited Element/Extension changes in the snapshot are recorded as out of scope rather than findings.

## Main migration themes
The wire representation remains a primitive string with optional primitive extensions; cardinality, element names, base definition, modifier flags, summary flags, and local semantic text are stable. Migration work is mainly for tooling that consumes StructureDefinitions directly: validators should understand the R6 regex and code generators should not mistake the corrected `markdown` metadata for a JSON wire-format change.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no Critical or High findings. The two local findings are Low impact: a widened lexical regex and a snapshot metadata correction relevant to code generation.

## Findings requiring human review
No finding requires mandatory human review, but the exact rationale for the regex change would be clearer with an official diff or datatype narrative page.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The regex change is backward-compatible for ordinary R4-to-R6 validation because it widens the accepted lexical space. The snapshot FHIR-type metadata change aligns generated metadata with the primitive's actual type and can be handled by preserving `markdown` as a string-like primitive alias in generated models.

## Follow-up analysis
The same regex change appears on the `string` base primitive and should be assessed in the separate `string` report for broad cross-primitive impact.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No hard instance-breaking change was found for `markdown`. The main migration concerns are rare R6 values that an R4 regex-based validator may reject, and StructureDefinition-driven code generators that react to `markdown.value` metadata changing from `string` to `markdown` in the snapshot. The largest uncertainty is the absence of an official diff and R6 regex extension definition in the local package.
summary.migrationThemesMd: `markdown` keeps the same canonical identity, primitive wire representation, base definition, element set, cardinalities, and local descriptive text. Migration should focus on validators and code generators rather than data transforms: update the lexical rule to the R6 regex, preserve markdown as a string-like primitive in APIs, and test cross-version conversion for unusual control-whitespace values.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural comparison because both assigned StructureDefinitions and package indexes were available locally and the R6 counterpart matched the expected canonical identity. Confidence in the impact of the regex change is slightly lower because the R6 package did not include the regex extension StructureDefinition and no official narrative/diff was consulted.

findings.title: markdown.value regex was widened to allow any non-empty string

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `markdown.value` used a regex character class that allowed non-whitespace plus explicit space, carriage return, line feed, and tab, with one or more characters required.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `markdown.value` uses an anchored pattern that accepts any character, whitespace or non-whitespace, while still requiring at least one character.

facts.oldValue: One or more characters from the R4 character class
facts.newValue: One or more characters of any kind
facts.note: This is a widening for R4-to-R6 validation, with possible R6-to-R4 rejection of unusual whitespace/control characters.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are unchanged (`markdown.value`), and the regex extension is on the same ElementDefinition type entry in both versions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4-valid markdown values should remain valid under the R6 regex because `^[\s\S]+$` accepts any non-empty string. The practical compatibility risk is the reverse direction: an R6 value containing characters outside R4's explicit whitespace set, such as form feed or vertical tab, may fail an R4 validator that enforces the R4 regex as a full-string lexical rule. This is expected to be rare for human-authored markdown.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: No direct clinical or business safety issue was identified; the risk is validation or conversion rejection of unusual text content.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that markdown is any non-empty string content and avoid excluding uncommon whitespace characters.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because the regex change widens the accepted lexical space.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal, accepting any non-empty markdown string rather than excluding uncommon characters, is reasonable on the available StructureDefinition evidence. This is not a hard R4-to-R6 break: R4-valid values remain accepted by the R6 regex, and the remaining concern is rare reverse conversion or strict R4 validation of unusual R6 values.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This finding is not a backward-compatible base-design alternative case in the primary R4-to-R6 direction. The R6 regex already preserves the R4 lexical space while widening it. Retaining the R4 regex would be a stricter reverse-compatibility choice for R6-to-R4 conversion, not a less-breaking R6 base design for existing R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping the R4 regex would improve rare R6-to-R4 reverse compatibility but would preserve the narrower lexical rule R6 appears to relax.

evidence.detail: The regex extension is defined in R4 as a regular expression that defines the syntax for the data element to be considered valid.

examples.examplesMd: The example is illustrative rather than a complete FHIR resource. It represents a markdown primitive value consisting only of U+000C FORM FEED, which is accepted by the R6 `^[\s\S]+$` regex but not by a strict full-string application of the R4 character class.

findings.narrativeMd: `markdown.value` changed from a narrower character-class regex to an anchored any-character regex. This does not invalidate ordinary existing R4 markdown, but it allows R6 producers to create unusual non-empty strings that an R4 validator may reject. The change matters mainly for strict cross-version validation and conversion pipelines, not for typical Markdown rendering.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid non-empty markdown string remains valid in R6 under the new regex. R6-valid content is not guaranteed to be R4-representable if it relies on characters outside the R4 regex's explicit class. Strict parsers that compile these regexes into generated validators should update tests for non-empty strings and unusual whitespace.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R4-to-R6 migration does not need to transform ordinary markdown values for this regex. R6-to-R4 conversion should either reject values outside the R4 lexical space, normalize/drop unacceptable control whitespace when policy permits, or document that the conversion is lossy. Validator test suites should include empty string, ordinary markdown, multiline markdown, tabbed markdown, and uncommon whitespace-only values.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because the change widens validation, it is already backward-compatible in the primary R4-to-R6 direction. The avoidable part is only the reverse-conversion risk: R6 could have retained the old regex to avoid rare R6-to-R4 mismatches, but that would keep excluding characters that the R6 ballot apparently intends to permit.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The same regex change appears on the `string` base primitive. This finding is scoped to the effective `markdown.value` rule because the markdown differential carries the regex in both versions; broad base-primitive impact should be owned by the `string` report.

findings.title: markdown.value snapshot FHIR type metadata now identifies markdown instead of string

oldState.summary: The R4 snapshot type entry used `structuredefinition-fhir-type` value `string`, even though the R4 differential used `markdown`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4's snapshot presented the primitive value's FHIR type metadata as `string`; the actual ElementDefinition type code still used FHIRPath `System.String` and the differential already identified the primitive as `markdown`.

newState.summary: The R6 snapshot and differential both use `structuredefinition-fhir-type` value `markdown`.
newState.narrativeMd: R6's snapshot now aligns this metadata with the primitive datatype name `markdown`, while keeping the underlying FHIRPath scalar type as `System.String`.

facts.note: The local differential did not change; the effective snapshot metadata changed.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same `markdown.value` element exists in both versions with unchanged path, cardinality, and FHIRPath type code. Only the snapshot's FHIR type metadata extension value differs.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This does not change JSON or XML instance representation: `markdown` remains a primitive string-like value. The risk is limited to tools that generate classes, serializers, schemas, or validators from the snapshot and treat the `structuredefinition-fhir-type` extension as the authoritative primitive type. Such tools may now produce or expect a distinct `markdown` primitive wrapper or alias instead of plain `string`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is tooling incompatibility rather than clinical semantic loss.

justification.inferredGoal: Make the snapshot metadata identify the actual primitive datatype instead of collapsing it to its string base.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: A less-breaking base design could have kept the legacy snapshot FHIR-type value as string while adding another markdown-specific metadata signal, but that would duplicate type metadata and leave ambiguity.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: the R6 snapshot aligns the metadata with the markdown primitive identity and the R4 differential, without changing JSON or XML wire representation. The compatibility impact is limited to StructureDefinition-driven tooling, and the less-breaking base-design alternative has material long-term ambiguity, so the change is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base-design alternative would not be ordinary generated-code aliasing; that is migration mitigation. A true base alternative would keep the R4 snapshot's string FHIR-type value for legacy consumers and add or clarify markdown-specific primitive identity through a second standard metadata signal. That would preserve many R4-era generators, but it would create duplicate type signals for the same primitive value and could cause validators, schemas, and generators to diverge indefinitely on which signal is authoritative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy snapshot-driven code generation, but weakens metadata fidelity and risks tools disagreeing over whether string or markdown is authoritative.

evidence.detail: R4 snapshot reports `string` as the FHIR type metadata.
R4 differential already reports `markdown`, showing that the snapshot value was not the only local metadata signal.
R6 snapshot reports `markdown` as the FHIR type metadata.

examples.examplesMd: No instance fragment is provided because this is not a wire-format change. A JSON element whose FHIR type is markdown is still serialized as a JSON string value with any primitive extensions in the sibling underscore element.

findings.narrativeMd: The R6 snapshot changes `markdown.value` metadata from the base `string` type label to the specific `markdown` primitive type label. This can surprise generators that used the R4 snapshot to map the value directly to a plain string type, but it should be treated as a metadata precision/correction rather than a change to how markdown appears in instances.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances do not become invalid, and R6 markdown instances remain string-valued on the wire. The affected compatibility surface is generated model shape, schema generation, reflection, and validator internals that consume snapshot type extensions. Tools should continue to recognize the underlying FHIRPath type code `http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate models and validators from the R6 package and inspect any API surface that changed from `string` to a `markdown` wrapper or alias. If source compatibility matters, provide overloads, implicit conversions, or type aliases so existing string-handling code continues to work while preserving the markdown-specific FHIR type in metadata.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The standards artifact could have preserved the R4 snapshot's `string` metadata to avoid generator churn, but that would keep the snapshot less precise than the differential and canonical primitive identity. A tool-level compatibility alias is the cleaner backward-compatible path.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind `primitive-type`, type `markdown`, derivation `specialization`, base `string`, abstract flag, and active status are stable. Package version, date, publisher, contacts, jurisdiction, generated narrative, and working-group metadata changed as expected for a new ballot package.

The differential still contains `markdown` and `markdown.value`; the snapshot still contains `markdown`, `markdown.id`, `markdown.extension`, and `markdown.value`. No local element addition, removal, rename, move, split, or merge was detected.
`markdown` remains `0..*`, `markdown.value` remains `0..1`, and inherited `id` and `extension` cardinalities are unchanged in the effective snapshot.

The actual ElementDefinition type code for `markdown.value` remains `http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String`. The snapshot's `structuredefinition-fhir-type` metadata change is covered separately as a code-generation finding.
`markdown` has no Reference-typed local elements and therefore no reference target list changes.
No terminology binding is present on `markdown` or `markdown.value`; no ValueSet or CodeSystem comparison is applicable.
No local invariant was added, removed, or strengthened for `markdown.value`. Snapshot changes to inherited `ele-1`/`ext-1` wording and XPath metadata are out of scope for this artifact.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value is present on the local markdown elements in either version.
`markdown`, `markdown.id`, `markdown.extension`, and `markdown.value` remain non-modifier elements in the snapshot.
The effective snapshot summary flags remain false for the markdown elements.
No local slicing is present on `markdown.value`; inherited extension slicing did not introduce a markdown-specific change.

The local root short, definition, and comment are unchanged, including the guidance that systems are not required to support markdown rendering and that the syntax is GFM. The top-level StructureDefinition description changed from `Base StructureDefinition for markdown type` to `markdown type`, which is metadata wording rather than a conformance change.

No JSON/XML wire-format representation changed: `markdown` remains a primitive string-like value and `markdown.value` remains represented as an XML attribute in the StructureDefinition. Code-generation metadata changes are reported separately.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds type-characteristics and governance metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds top-level metadata extensions such as `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` values `has-size` and `do-translations`, plus working-group, jurisdiction, contact, `experimental=false`, and generated narrative metadata. These do not add, remove, or constrain instance elements.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tooling that reads StructureDefinition metadata may start treating `markdown` as size-bearing and translation-relevant. This is useful for UI, documentation, and localization workflows, but it is not a validation break for existing instances.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Publisher and top-level description wording changed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The publisher changed from `HL7 FHIR Standard` to `HL7 International / FHIR Infrastructure`, and the top-level description no longer starts with `Base StructureDefinition for`. The local ElementDefinition definition and comment for markdown semantics are unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation generators may display different package metadata, but validators and instance converters should not treat this as a datatype semantics change.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: The same regex widening appears on the `string` base primitive. A separate `string` analysis should own the broad cross-primitive impact and de-duplication of any inherited/base behavior.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff or change note was available locally, so inferred rationale for the regex and metadata changes is based on the computable StructureDefinitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Consult an official HL7 diff, ballot change log, or Jira item for markdown/string primitive changes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 package index did not include a `StructureDefinition-regex` artifact, even though the regex extension URL appears in the R6 markdown StructureDefinition. The validation mechanism was therefore inferred from the R4 extension definition and its continued use in the R6 artifact.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Locate the R6 definition or replacement documentation for `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/regex`, or confirm from the R6 build process how validators should interpret the extension.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The local computable artifacts preserve the GFM wording, but the R6 narrative datatype page was not checked for additional conformance prose about markdown rendering, translations, or size semantics.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the R6 ballot narrative page for primitive datatypes and markdown.
